docs.title: COMPAS CEM
docs.text:
The combinatorial equilibrium method (CEM) for COMPAS.

Constrained form-finding of a spiral staircase.

The CEM is a numerical form-finding method that automatically generates forms in static equilibrium for spatial structures modeled as 3D bar systems. These systems resist external loads purely under tensile and compressive axial forces, leading to mechanically efficient structural configurations. COMPAS CEM encapsulates the CEM into an open-source structural design tool that enables the formulation and the solution of constrained form-finding problems in plain and simple Python code.

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
• Mix tension and compression forces: Explore a wider spectrum of structural typologies by combining internal tension and compression forces in the same structure. Design space frames, bridges, tensegrities, and staircases and go beyond the conventional catalog of compression-only shells and cable-nets!

  • Solve constrained form-finding problems efficiently via automatic differentiation: Generate forms in static equilibrium that simultaneously meet a priori design goals such as best-fitting a global target shape, restraining bar lengths, and controlling the reaction forces at the supports of a structure.

  • Usable across different 3D modeling software and operating systems: COMPAS CEM runs on Windows, MacOS and Linux (perhaps one day also in the metaverse) and it does not depend on any CAD software to work. However, it provides the necessary interfaces to be seamlessly used inside popular design environments like Rhino, Blender, and Grasshopper. As a COMPAS extension, COMPAS CEM offers native integration and data exchange with other extensions and plugins in the COMPAS ecosystem.

  • Move those sliders with the Grasshopper plugin: Are you a Grasshopper person? Worry not. COMPAS CEM is shipped too as a precooked Grasshopper plugin to readily integrate our constrained form-finding engine into your next spaghetti pipeline 🍝.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Added the COMPAS CEM logo, a self-stressed structure form-found with CEM: a tension hexagon holding two compression triangles through six compression spokes, with no loads and reactions. Every member is drawn with a width proportional to its force, red in tension and blue in compression, the closed cells are lightly filled and inset from the members, and every node is a white dot. Where two members cross without a node, the upper one cuts a halo of whitespace into the lower one. The logo comes in three weights with the same proportions: thin for large and vector use, regular for mid sizes, and a bare icon without cells or nodes for 40 px and below, where those details no longer resolve. scripts/logo/build_logo.py rebuilds every SVG, PDF and transparent PNG in docs/assets/logo from the form diagram beside it. The logo replaces the COMPAS-style mark as the docs logo and favicon, on the docs home page, as the Rhino Package Manager icon, and in the Info component's icon. The header logo sits on white, since its compression blue would vanish on the blue header.
  • Added an Auxiliary Trail Settings component in grasshopper, in the toolbar group of Assemble Topology Diagram, that sets the auxiliary trails it adds: length for every auxiliary trail edge, state for the sign of its force, and vector for the direction of its support in the topology drawing. Assemble Topology Diagram takes them through a new last input, auxiliary_trails_settings, named after add_auxiliary_trails, and add_auxiliary_trails stays the switch, so wired settings alone add nothing and show a remark. Added AuxiliaryTrailSettings to compas_cem.ghpython, the frozen dataclass the component outputs, which rejects a non-positive length, a zero state and a zero vector. The length and the state are global, so every auxiliary trail takes the same; Grasshopper had no way to set them, and scripts edited the auxiliary edges after building the trails.
  • Added TopologyDiagram.align_trails, which shifts every trail so that as many deviation edges as possible are direct, and a topology without indirect deviation edges solves in a single iteration. A deviation edge between two trails fixes how far apart their starting sequences must be, so the method places the trails in one walk over the trail pairs: between every pair, the gap most of their edges agree on wins, and the pairs with the most agreeing edges are placed first, so the order in which edges were added does not decide which ones stay indirect. Every group of linked trails then starts at sequence 0. The loops that shifted a trail whenever one of its deviation edges was indirect could not tell an unfinished alignment from an impossible one, so on a braced topology they stretched the sequences until their pass limit, and those that only looked at origin nodes missed edges between interior nodes.
  • Added an auto_align toggle to Shift Trails, off by default, which aligns every trail with align_trails and warns about the deviation edges that stay indirect. It works in place of origin_node_keys and sequences: the component warns and outputs nothing when both are given, and when neither is.
  • Added compas_cem.ghpython.cross_lines, the lines of the cross that marks a loaded node, which Draw Topology and the viewer both draw.
  • Added topology_drawing with TopologyDrawing and StyledPolyline to compas_cem.ghpython, the style rules of Draw Topology in plain Python, and TopologyPreview, its Rhino geometry. Draw Form's and Draw Topology's rules share diagram_display.py, and their previews diagram_preview.py.
  • Added LOAD_CROSS_SIZE to compas_cem: how far a load cross reaches from its node, as a fraction of the diagram's bounding-box diagonal.
  • Added a Form Display Settings component in grasshopper that sets how Draw Form draws a form: arrow_min for the smallest load or reaction magnitude to draw as an arrow, compared before the scale applies, and arrow_scale for the length of the arrows, both named after the arrows they set so neither reads as a bound on the edge forces, width_min and width_max for the edge widths in pixels, and radius_min and radius_max for the pipe radii in model units, radius_max also sizing the thickened nodes. Its settings output is a frozen dataclass rather than a named tuple, since Grasshopper unpacks a tuple output into its items.
  • Added ARROW_HEADPORTION, ARROW_HEADWIDTH and ARROW_BODYWIDTH to compas_cem, the arrow proportions as fractions of an arrow's length (head length, head radius, body radius), with _2D variants for the plotter, whose widths are full widths as matplotlib takes them. Every engine draws its arrows with them.
  • Added form_drawing, FormDisplaySettings, edge_widths, edge_radii and reaction_shifts to compas_cem.ghpython: the style rules of Draw Form in plain Python, testable outside Rhino. Added FormPreview, which turns them into Rhino geometry once per solution so a viewport redraw only loops over Rhino objects.
  • Added TopologyDiagram.auxiliary_support_nodes, which yields the support nodes that end the auxiliary trails, not their origin nodes.
  • Added an is_absolute flag to every optimization parameter. With is_absolute=True, bound_low and bound_up are the values the parameter may take instead of distances from its start value, and edge bounds are signed, negative in compression. It defaults to False and is saved with the parameter's data, so scripts and files that predate it keep their relative bounds.
  • Added Optimizer.check_start_bounds, which solve runs first: a parameter whose start value lies outside its bounds raises a ValueError naming the parameter, its start value and its bounds, where NLopt raised a bare invalid_argument. Absolute bounds can exclude the start value; relative bounds always contain it.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Made build_trails place every auxiliary support along auxiliary_trail_vector whatever the sign of auxiliary_trail_length, and turned the default vector to (-1, -1, -1), so a topology with the default negative length draws as before. A negative length reversed the vector, so a direction chosen for the drawing flipped with the state. Only the topology drawing moves, since the solver places every auxiliary support along the residual force of its node; a topology with a positive length and the default vector now draws its auxiliary supports on the other side.
  • Added a bake input to Draw Form and Draw Topology. Wired to a Button, every press adds the drawing to the Rhino document as one undo step, each category on its own sublayer of COMPAS CEM::Form or COMPAS CEM::Topology. Lines bake with their colors and plot weights, loads and reactions with an arrowhead, deviation edges with Rhino's dashed linetype, loaded only if the document lacks one, and thickened meshes with their colors and a render material of the same color, named after its hex code and reused across bakes, since rendered views shade a mesh with its material rather than its display color. Labels, the support and origin nodes, which repeat nodes, and the trails, which repeat trail edges, are not baked. The outputs' model objects cannot carry arrowheads or linetypes, and a Line or Curve parameter keeps only the geometry, so baking from the outputs lost what the button keeps.
  • Added thick_sides to Form Display Settings, the number of faces around every thickened pipe, arrow and node sphere, 8 by default and at least 3.
  • Revised the descriptions and docstrings of the Grasshopper components: the draw components' outputs explain where their colors survive, the toggles read as "Whether to…", every code docstring matches its component's description, and duplicated, misspelled and misattributed descriptions are fixed.
  • Added decompose, show_loads, show_reactions, show_forces and show_keys toggles to Draw Form. decompose, on by default, draws every load and reaction force as up to three arrows, one per x, y and z component, each placed and cleared like a whole arrow, and skips a component smaller than arrow_min. show_loads and show_reactions, on by default, hide their category everywhere: it neither previews nor bakes, and its output is empty, so the outputs always match the drawing. The names match the form plotter's. show_forces, off by default, labels every drawn edge with its force in the viewport only. show_keys, off by default, labels the drawn nodes and edges with their keys as Draw Topology does, and an edge shown with both gets one label, u-v: force, so the two never overlap. Each name says what its labels show. The toggles sit on Draw Form rather than in Form Display Settings, since a toggle is reached for more often than the settings. FormDisplaySettings keeps all of them as fields, so a script sets every display option in one place, and Draw Form sets them from its toggles.
  • Made Trail Edge and Deviation Edge warn when a line is connected but an input they need is missing, where they returned nothing silently: Trail Edge without a length or a plane, or with a length but no state; Deviation Edge without a state or a force. Components already placed in a definition keep their old code.
  • Made the viewer skip a force arrow without length, from a zero scale or a zero force, which has no axis to build its cylinder and cone on. Draw Form now draws a form without edges, and the viewer a topology without nodes, where both raised on an empty sequence.
  • Made Draw Topology draw the topology in color, with the topology plotter's defaults: nodes by type (supports green, origin nodes purple, the rest light gray), edges by the state their length or force sets (blue in compression, red in tension, auxiliary trails orange), deviation edges always dashed, and a black cross at every loaded node. Its outputs keep their names and become Rhino 8 model objects that bake with their colors and a 2 px plot weight, drawn by the component with their default preview off, as Draw Form's are. loads now holds the crosses, two lines per loaded node in the XY plane, so it bakes what is drawn; the load lines are gone, along with force_min and force_scale. Deviation edges are dashed in the viewport, and bake dashed through the bake input. A show_keys toggle, off by default, labels the drawn nodes with their keys and the drawn edges with u-v, in the viewport only. Components already placed in a definition keep their inputs and outputs.
  • Made the viewer mark the loaded nodes of a topology with the same crosses instead of arrows, as the topology plotter and Draw Topology do.
  • Made Draw Form draw the form in color. Edges are red in tension and blue in compression, with widths spread linearly over the settings' bounds by absolute force across the whole form, so a selection keeps its widths. Free nodes are light gray, so they show against a white background, and supports green; loads are green and reactions gray, drawn as lines halfway between the width bounds that end in Rhino's own arrowhead, sized on screen as Grasshopper draws a vector; a shaded cone read as a solid in a line drawing. A selected Draw Form takes Grasshopper's selection color.
  • Made Draw Form's outputs Rhino 8 model objects that carry each item's color and plot weight. The outputs keep their names and still plug into Line, Curve and Point inputs, which keep the geometry only; a Model Object or Data parameter keeps the attributes too. The plot weight is the pixel width at 96 dpi, so Print Display shows baked lines at their preview width. Model objects drop curve arrowheads, so a load or reaction collected from an output bakes as a plain line.
  • Made Draw Form draw its own outputs and switch their default preview off on every solve, since Grasshopper's preview ignores per-item colors. The component's Preview switches the drawing on and off. Grasshopper does not bake hidden outputs, so the right-click Bake of Draw Form and Draw Topology does nothing; their bake input does the baking instead. A data type written in Python could preview and bake per output, but Grasshopper cannot convert it into Line or Curve inputs, which would break definitions that pipe the edges.
  • Added a thicken input to Draw Form, off by default. When on, the nodes become spheres of radius radius_max, the edges capped pipe meshes whose radii spread by absolute force over the settings' radius_min and radius_max, and the loads and reactions solid arrows. Every output then holds meshes, which bake with their colors, so a definition that expects points or lines downstream must keep thicken off. A sphere is as wide as the widest pipe, every pipe stops one sphere radius short of its nodes, since a sphere is meshed with flat faces inside its true surface and a pipe trimmed only to meet the true sphere still poked through, and the arrows move along their own direction by the sphere radius, back when they end at a node and ahead when they start at it, so neither end hides inside a sphere. The meshes are merged into one per color for drawing; a solve with 10,000 edges builds them in about 0.35 s.
  • Gave every arrow the same proportions, as fractions of its length, so the CEM engines draw forces alike. The plotter draws matplotlib FancyArrow patches in one collection, in place of compas_plotter's arrows of a fixed screen size. The viewer draws a cylinder body and a cone head, in place of compas_viewer's vectors. Draw Form uses the same cone in both modes.
  • Made every load arrow end at its node, so its head touches the node it loads, in the plotter, the viewer, Draw Form and the load lines of Draw Topology. Loads started at their node and pointed away, which read as a force leaving it. Reactions keep their rule: they end at a support they push into.
  • Moved Draw Form's force_min and force_scale into Form Display Settings, renamed arrow_min and arrow_scale, and corrected the form description, which called it a topology diagram. Components already placed in a definition keep their inputs and plain outputs.
  • Made FormDiagramObject take its reaction shifts from the shared reaction_shifts.
  • Renamed Edge Forces and Lengths to Edge Forces and removed its lengths output, which returned the stored signed length whose sign follows the force and confused post-processing. forces stays signed, negative in compression. Unsigned lengths come from the Length component on Draw Form's edges, which follow the same edge_keys. Components already placed in a definition keep both outputs.
  • Added a filter_auxiliary input to Disassemble Topology in grasshopper. When True, every output leaves out the auxiliary trails, their edges and their support nodes: auxiliary_trail_keys comes out empty, trail_keys loses only the auxiliary trails, and sequence_keys loses the auxiliary support nodes but keeps every sequence, an emptied one as an empty tuple, so a tuple's position stays its sequence number, as the library already does for sequences without nodes. Origin nodes stay, since an auxiliary trail starts at a node of the structure.
  • Added a toggle as the first input of the JSON components: read on Import Topology Diagram and Import Form Diagram, export on Export Diagram, so a file is read or written only on demand. While it is off, the components output nothing; Export Diagram outputs data only on the run that writes the file. import is a Python keyword, so it cannot name an input.
  • Made the bounds of the eight Grasshopper parameter components absolute: they now set is_absolute=True, since bounds relative to the start value were hard to read. Components already placed in a definition keep their relative bounds. Corrected the node key description of the three load parameter components, which named an origin node where any loaded node applies.
  • Added a state input under line to the Trail Edge and Deviation Edge components. Its sign sets tension (positive) or compression (negative), the components take only the absolute value of length and force, and a zero state raises a warning. Trail Edge takes either a length or a plane, with a warning when both are connected; with a plane, state is optional and signs the unit length Trail Edge stores, so the topology records the intended state and Draw Topology colors the edge by it; the plane's position still ends the trail when the form is found, and the length applies only to a trail that never meets the plane. An unsigned placeholder drew every compression trail ending at a plane in red.
  • Corrected the TrailEdge docstring and the Trail Edge plane description, which said a plane keeps the length's sign. The solver replaces the signed length with the distance to the plane, so the plane's position sets the state, and the length applies only if the trail runs parallel to the plane.
  • Called the CEM the combinatorial equilibrium method instead of the Combinatorial Equilibrium Modeling framework, as the repository description does: in the README and the documentation's home page, which now describe the 3D bar systems it models and their purely axial forces, and in the site description, the PyPI summary, the package docstring, the yak manifest, the software citation and the Colors component's description.
  • Raised the Grasshopper components' compas_cem requirement to the current version and added it to bump-my-version, so every release raises it, with test_component_headers to catch a stale header. Rhino upgrades the library only when the requirement rises above the version it holds, so under the 0.9.1 plugin a Rhino holding 0.9.0 kept it and Info reported v0.9.0.
  • Switched the license metadata to PEP 639: an SPDX license = "MIT" and license-files = ["LICENSE", "AUTHORS.md"] replace the license table and the License :: classifier, which setuptools deprecates and stops supporting in builds from 2027-02-18. The build now requires setuptools 77.0.3: 77.0 added the fields, 77.0.0 and 77.0.2 have no files on PyPI, and 77.0.3 fixed their first bugs. The wheel and sdist ship the same two license files as before, which setuptools' default globs already picked up, and their metadata now reads License-Expression: MIT.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Added uv instructions: uv add and uv pip install in the installation guide and the README, and uv sync --extra dev with uv run for contributors, pinned by a committed uv.lock. .gitignore excluded the lock on the belief that it would pin every CI job, but CI installs with pip, and uv's pip interface ignores a lock anyway. The pip commands stay as the fallback, and CI still installs with pip. The development tools stay in the dev extra rather than dependency groups, because compas-actions installs .[dev].
  • Added an icon for each Grasshopper component, replacing the CEM logo all 38 shared; Info keeps the logo. Each component folder holds the TikZ source icon.tex beside its icon.png, and components_cpython/icon_style.tex holds the shared palette, group tiles and styles. The icons follow the conventions of the CEM diagrams and the Grasshopper icon guide's empty border and drop shadow. Each tile is framed in a dark shade of its group's color, since a light frame washed out in Grasshopper.
  • Added the build-icons task, which renders each icon.tex into a 24 px icon.png with its drop shadow. It needs pdflatex and pdftocairo; the icons are committed, so building the plugin does not.
  • Added pillow to the dev extra, which tasks.py imports for the drop shadow.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Refreshed .editorconfig from the 2021 template so editors agree with the pre-commit hooks: two-space indentation now covers .yaml as well as .yml, Python uses ruff's 88 columns, and the Markdown and LICENSE exceptions, which the whitespace and end-of-file hooks undo, are gone with the Makefile and Windows script sections that matched no file.
  • Limited uv.lock to Python 3.11 and newer through [tool.uv] environments. Resolved for 3.9 and 3.10 too, the lock pinned releases of Pillow, filelock, urllib3, cryptography and other development and plotting dependencies that have no security fix for those Pythons, which opened about a hundred Dependabot alerts. The package still supports Python 3.9, CI still tests 3.9 to 3.13 with pip, and work on 3.9 or 3.10 uses the pip route.
  • Extended the copyright years in LICENSE from 2020-2021 to 2020-2026, and set compas_cem.__copyright__ to the license's holder with no year. It read Copyright 2020 - Princeton University.
  • Moved every workflow to actions/checkout@v7 and actions/setup-python@v7. The dev-docs job still ran the deprecated Node 20 releases checkout@v4 and setup-python@v5.
  • Replaced the Zomzog/changelog-checker action, unmaintained since 2022 and declaring the retired node12 runtime, with a shell step that lists the pull request's changed files with gh pr diff --name-only. The no changelog label still skips it.
  • Replaced the warning that the Grasshopper plugin is not installable with Package Manager instructions for Rhino 8 in the README and the installation guide. 0.9.0 ships the plugin on the Rhino package server, so the 0.9.0 README on PyPI still carries the outdated warning.
  • Pointed the README's links to the examples, the API reference and the citing page at the latest documentation instead of dev, now that 0.9.0 is published.
  • Shrank the header animation to 960 by 540 pixels at 12 frames per second, 4.4 MB, from 1280 by 720 at 24 frames per second and 13.5 MB. PyPI loads README images through an image proxy, so the 0.9.0 page shows a broken image: GitHub's raw file host labels a file that large application/octet-stream, and such proxies refuse non-image types and files over about 5 MB, as GitHub's own proxy does for the larger file.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text: • Removed the last conda references: the conda.recipe/ line in .gitignore and conda as a virtual environment example in CONTRIBUTING.md. Every dependency installs with pip.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Added pyproject.toml, replacing setup.py, setup.cfg, pytest.ini and .bumpversion.cfg.
  • Added mkdocs.yml and a mkdocs-material documentation site.
  • Added .github/workflows/pr-checks.yml.
  • Added regression baselines for every example under tests/baseline, captured from 0.8.6 behaviour.
  • Added regression tests that add_node and add_edge accept both vocabularies, reject a mismatched element, and survive a JSON round trip and a copy().
  • Added Diagram.node_connected_edges, which returns the edges incident to a node.
  • Added TopologyDiagram.__from_data__, which restores the integer keys of the trail bookkeeping after a round trip.
  • Added regression tests that trails and auxiliary trails survive a JSON round trip.
  • Added plotters/scene_objects.py and viewers/scene_objects.py, replacing the artist and object modules of both visualization backends.
  • Added tests/baseline/render.py, which renders every example headless for visual review of the plotters.
  • Added ghpython/scene_objects.py, replacing ghpython/artists.py with compas.scene scene objects that register themselves in the Grasshopper context.
  • Added src/compas_cem/ghpython/yak_template/, holding the manifest.yml and the package icon that yakerize wraps the built components with.
  • Added the build_cpython_ghuser_components, update_gh_header, yakerize and publish_yak tasks to tasks.py, together with the ghuser_cpython and yak configuration blocks they read.
  • Added a static instanceGuid to all 39 component metadata.json files. The componentizer mints a fresh random GUID whenever the field is absent, so every build emitted different GUIDs and broke the components already placed in a .gh file.
  • Added a dev-docs job that publishes the documentation built from main as the dev version. compas-actions.docs deploys mkdocs on a version tag only, so between releases the site would otherwise show the last release and nothing newer.
  • Added a concurrency group to the build, docs and pull request workflows, so pushing to a pull request cancels its own in-flight run instead of queueing a second one. Pushes and tags keep a run-unique group, so a stuck run cannot hold up a deploy.
  • Added workflow_dispatch to the build and docs workflows, so either can be run by hand.
  • Added the yak publish to the release workflow. After the PyPI upload, which the components' # r: header installs from, it packages the components with invoke yakerize and pushes them with invoke publish-yak, authenticated by the YAK_TOKEN secret. compas-actions.publish only builds the components, so no release had reached the Rhino package server. The push cannot be rehearsed on the test server: it is wiped each night and keeps its own records, so it rejects the API key that yak login --ci issues on the production server. A manual run that pushed there built and packaged the components on Windows, then failed with a 401.
  • Added a viz extra, read from requirements-viz.txt, holding compas_plotter>=1.0.1 and compas_viewer>=2.0, the backends of compas_cem.plotters and compas_cem.viewers. They stay out of the core install so that compas_cem stays lean inside Rhino 8, where the viewer would otherwise pull in PySide6 and PyOpenGL for nothing. The dev extra includes them. Importing either module without them raises an ImportError that names the extra.
  • Added a Made with COMPAS badge and a badge linking to the Computer-Aided Design article underpinning the framework to README.md.
  • Added a pre-commit configuration with ruff check and format, whitespace, end-of-file, YAML, TOML, JSON and merge-conflict checks, and a check that fails when a personal name appears in project prose outside the authorship files, or in a commit message. invoke lint runs ruff check --fix on src and tests only and never checks formatting, so the hook is the only check on formatting, examples and tasks.py. A pre-commit job in the pull request checks runs every hook on every file, so these checks also gate merges; commit messages are checked locally only.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Migrated from COMPAS 1.17.10 to compas>=2.15,<3.0.
  • Rewrote the installation instructions around pip and venv. conda is being phased out across the COMPAS ecosystem, and compas no longer needs installing separately because compas_cem declares it.
  • Marked the Grasshopper plugin as not installable in this release. It linked into Rhino 6 and 7 through compas_rhino.install, which COMPAS 2 removed.
  • Renamed Constraint to Goal throughout, a clean break with no deprecation aliases. The nine concrete classes, the VectorConstraint and FloatConstraint bases, the constraints module, Optimizer.add_constraint and remove_constraint, and the eight Grasshopper component directories all follow. This frees the name Constraint for genuine hard constraints, which nlopt supports and the package does not yet use.
  • Made Diagram.add_node and Diagram.add_edge accept either a node or edge element, or a key with attributes. COMPAS 2 deserializes a graph by replaying add_node(key=, attr_dict=) and add_edge(u, v, attr_dict=), which the object-taking overrides shadowed, breaking copy() and from_json(). Both entry points now dispatch on the argument, so the authoring API is unchanged and deserialization reaches the base graph.
  • Made the entry points reject a mismatched element rather than silently treating it as a node key: add_node refuses an edge element, add_edge refuses a node element, and a key given both positionally and by name raises.
  • Folded NodeMixins and EdgeMixins into Diagram and dropped compas_cem.data.Data from its bases. Datastructure.__inheritance__ walks the MRO up to Datastructure calling __clstype__() on every class in between, so a plain object mixin made to_json() raise.
  • Changed the tol diagram attribute from a format string to an integer count of decimal places, following compas.tolerance.TOL.geometric_key.
  • Ported serialization from the data property pair to __data__ and __from_data__ on goals and on edge and node parameters.
  • Gave Goal, Parameter, EdgeParameter and NodeParameter default constructor arguments, so __from_data__ can build one without knowing the concrete signature.
  • Regenerated examples/03_bridge_2d.json, which was COMPAS 1.7.1 JSON and unreadable by COMPAS 2. Node and edge insertion order is preserved, because it sets the order of the optimizer's parameter vector.
  • Changed requires-python from >=3.8 to >=3.9,<3.14, and both CI matrices to 3.9 through 3.13, now that the distutils ceiling is gone. The floor is 3.9 because Rhino 8 runs CPython 3.9 and every Grasshopper component installs this package into it; a 3.10 floor made that install fail. The macOS cell for 3.9 is left out because compas-actions.build skips it without running anything.
  • Replaced the reStructuredText module docstrings and inline markup with Markdown, and moved parameter and return types out of docstrings and into the signature position that mkdocstrings renders.
  • Migrated the plotters from compas_plotters artists to compas_plotter>=1.0.1 scene objects, and the viewers from compas_view2 objects to compas_viewer>=2.0 scene objects. Both register through compas.scene.register on import, because compas discovers scene object plugins in compas* packages only.
  • Pinned the plotter node size policy to relative. The upstream scene object defaults to absolute, which divides the node size by the plotter resolution instead of the node count and draws markers two orders of magnitude smaller.
  • Drew the topology load crosses straight onto the canvas. A line scene object fixes its own stacking order in its constructor, which put the crosses underneath the opaque node markers.
  • Fixed state_format in both visualization backends reading an undefined edge instead of the edge it was passed.
  • Fixed DiagramObject referring to self.topology, which it never defined.
  • Fixed a show_nodes setter that assigned to _show_edges.
  • Fixed DiagramArtist.draw_reactions documenting a min_load parameter that its signature calls min_force, and TopologyDiagramObject documenting its argument as form_diagram.
  • Renamed ghpython/components/ to ghpython/components_cpython/, matching compas_fab and the CPython-only component format that Rhino 8 loads.
  • Named every Grasshopper component <name> (COMPAS CEM) instead of COMPAS CEM: <name>. The componentizer only knows a prefix, so the suffix lives in each metadata.json name and the prefix settings in tasks.py and release.yml are gone. The instance GUIDs are unchanged, so components already placed in a definition still resolve.
  • Renamed the Form Artist and Topology Artist components to Draw Form and Draw Topology, and the 08_Artists subcategory to 08_Visualization. Their directories are now CompasCem_DrawForm, CompasCem_DrawTopology and CompasCem_Colors. COMPAS 2 replaced artists with scene objects, so the artist vocabulary was legacy. The instance GUIDs are unchanged. A plotter docstring and the quick start example drop the word too.
  • Made the Constrained Form-Finding component solve in-process. Rhino 8 runs CPython, so nlopt and autograd run inside Rhino and the component drives Optimizer directly, as the Python examples do.

  • Annotated component inputs as optional where Grasshopper passes None for an unconnected input, under from __future__ import annotations so that Rhino 8, which is CPython 3.9, does not evaluate the unions at definition time.
  • Read node positions in the Grasshopper scene objects from the scene object rather than from the diagram, so a transformation set on the object applies to everything it draws.
  • Built the documentation on Python 3.12 instead of the compas-actions.docs default of 3.10. On 3.10 the resolver pairs pymdown-extensions 12, whose highlighter gained a required argument, with mkdocstrings 1.0.6, the last release for 3.10, which does not pass it, so every API page fails to render.
  • Moved the release publish job from ubuntu-latest to windows-latest and gave it the component-building inputs, because the componentizer loads GH_IO.dll.
  • Fixed _draw_forces normalizing a force vector before testing its magnitude, which divided by a zero length at a node carrying no load or reaction.
  • Fixed the Draw Form and Draw Topology components passing their diagram positionally to the scene object. The first parameter of a COMPAS 2 graph scene object is show_nodes, so the diagram never reached the object and every draw failed on a None graph. Both now pass it as item.
  • Fixed the Export Diagram component returning diagram.data, which COMPAS 2 replaced with __data__, so it raised after writing the file. It now returns the JSON string it wrote, from to_jsonstring, which from_jsonstring can read back.
  • Fixed draw_reactions raising on a node with no connected edge, where it searched an empty sequence for the strongest edge force.
  • Fixed the topology JSON import component declaring a class named FormDiagramFromJSON and documenting itself as importing a form diagram.
  • Fixed a typeHinID misspelling in the Draw Topology component's metadata.json, which left two of its inputs without a type hint.
  • Replaced rs.AddPoint in the support node results component with point_to_rhino. The rhinoscriptsyntax call bakes a point into the Rhino document instead of returning geometry to the component output.
  • Returned an empty list rather than None from the topology draw methods when a selection is empty.
  • Fixed the five Python example pages showing --8 < --"examples/…" instead of the example source. A pymdownx snippet marker is valid python, so ruff format reformatted it as an expression inside the fenced block and the include stopped resolving. Markdown is now excluded from the formatter.

  • Updated CI to compas-actions.build@v5, compas-actions.docs@v5 and compas-actions.publish@v3.
  • Replaced the Zenodo badge in README.md with a static shields.io badge on the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.5705740, which always resolves to the latest deposit. The badge Zenodo generates is rendered on request and frequently times out behind the GitHub image proxy, so it showed up broken.

The documentation links pointed at Sphinx pages the mkdocs site does not have, and the COMPAS tutorial and API links at pages COMPAS 2 moved. The build badge uses the current workflow badge URL.

docs.title: Install COMPAS CEM
docs.text:
compas_cem is on PyPI, and it pulls in everything it needs to model, form-find and optimize, compas among them. Install it with a one-liner:

pip install compas-cem

To draw diagrams with compas_cem.plotters or compas_cem.viewers, as the examples do, install the viz extra instead:

pip install "compas-cem[viz]"

The plotter and the viewer are optional so that compas_cem stays lean inside Rhino, which needs neither of them.

If you manage your project with uv, declare it as a dependency of that project instead:

uv add "compas-cem[viz]"

To install it into an existing virtual environment without a project, use uv's pip interface:

uv pip install "compas-cem[viz]"

Note

compas_cem supports Python 3.9 to 3.13. The floor is 3.9 because that is the Python that Rhino 8 runs.

To double-check that everything is up and running, type the following in the command line and hit enter:

python -c "import compas_cem"

If no errors show up, celebrate 🎉! You have a working installation of compas_cem.

docs.title: Install the Grasshopper Plugin
docs.text:
There will be times when modeling a complex structure is easier to do with a few mouse-clicks instead of a hundred lines of code. The Grasshopper (GH) version of compas_cem lets you use all the important bits of our constrained form-finding engine in a (familiar) visual programming environment.

The plugin runs in Rhino 8 and ships on the Rhino package server:

  1. In Rhino 8, run the PackageManager command.
  2. Search for compas_cem and install it.
  3. Restart Rhino. The components appear under the COMPAS CEM tab in Grasshopper.

The first component you run installs the compas-cem Python package and its dependencies into Rhino's own Python, so that first run needs an internet connection and can take a minute.

Note

Rhino 6 and 7 are no longer supported. Their last compatible release is 0.8.6, which installs through COMPAS 1.

docs.title: Set up a development environment
docs.text:
To work on compas_cem itself, clone the repository and let uv set up the environment. It installs a matching Python, the package in editable mode, the plotter, the viewer and every development tool, pinned by the committed uv.lock, in one step:

git clone https://github.com/arpastrana/compas_cem.git
cd compas_cem
uv sync --extra dev
uv run invoke test

Prefix commands with uv run and they execute inside the project environment, with no activation step. A bare uv sync installs only the runtime dependencies, the same as pip install -e ..

The lock covers Python 3.11 to 3.13. To work on Python 3.9 or 3.10, the Python that Rhino 8 runs, or if you prefer pip, create and activate a virtual environment and install the same extra:

pip install -e ".[dev]"

See the contributing guide for the rest of the workflow.

docs.title: Update COMPAS CEM
docs.text:
If you installed compas_cem one day in the past and you want to update it to the latest available version, the update command is the following:

pip install --upgrade compas-cem

With uv, uv pip install --upgrade compas-cem does the same in a plain virtual environment, and uv lock --upgrade-package compas-cem followed by uv sync does it in a uv project.

Alternatively, if you want to switch to a specific version, for example version 0.8.6, type this:

pip install compas-cem==0.8.6

add_edge(edge=None, v=None, attr_dict=None, **kwattr)

Add an edge to the diagram, from an edge element or from two node keys.

Parameters:

  • edge –

    An edge element, or the first node of the edge given positionally.

  • v –

    The second node of the edge, when the first was given as a key.

  • attr_dict –

    The attributes to store on the edge.

  • **kwattr –

    Extra attributes to store on the edge.

Returns:

  • key –

    The two node keys of the added edge.

Notes

This accepts both vocabularies, as add_node does. An edge element carries its own attributes and may name its end nodes by coordinates, creating them if no node sits there yet.

    Parameters

        An edge element, or the first node of the edge given positionally.
    v :

def add_node(self, node=None, key=None, attr_dict=None, **kwattr):
    """
    Add a node to the diagram, from a node element or from a key.

    Parameters
    ----------
    node :
        A node element, or a node key given positionally.
    key :
        A node key. If `None`, the next available key is assigned.
    attr_dict :
        The attributes to store on the node.
    **kwattr :
        Extra attributes to store on the node.

    Returns
    -------
    key :
        The key of the added node.

    Notes
    -----
    This accepts both vocabularies. A node element carries its own
    coordinates and is indexed by its geometric key, which is how a diagram
    is authored. A bare key with attributes is how the base graph adds a
    node, and how deserialization replays one.
    """
    if isinstance(node, Node):
        return self._add_node_element(node)

    if isinstance(node, Edge):
        raise TypeError("an edge element must be added with add_edge")

    if node is not None:
        if key is not None:
            raise ValueError("a node key was given both positionally and by name")
        key = node

    if isinstance(key, Data):
        raise TypeError(f"{key!r} is not a node key")

    return super(Diagram, self).add_node(key=key, attr_dict=attr_dict, **kwattr)

def node_connected_edges(self, node):
    """
    The edges incident to a node.

    Parameters
    ----------
    node :
        A node key.

    Returns
    -------
    edges :
        The keys of the edges connected to the node.

    Notes
    -----
    Each edge is reported in the direction it is stored in, so that the key
    returned here can be used to look edge attributes up directly.
    """
    edges = []

    for neighbor in self.neighbors(node):
        if neighbor in self.edge[node]:
            edges.append((node, neighbor))
        else:
            edges.append((neighbor, node))

    return edges

@classmethod
def from_topology_diagram(cls, topology):
    """
    Construct a form diagram from a topology diagram.

    Parameters
    ----------
    topology :
        The topology diagram to copy.

    Returns
    -------
    form :
        A form diagram with the same nodes and edges as the topology.

    Notes
    -----
    The trail bookkeeping is dropped, because a form diagram is the result
    of walking the trails rather than a description of them.
    """
    form = topology.copy(cls=cls)

    del form.attributes["_trails"]
    del form.attributes["_auxiliary_trails"]
    del form.attributes["_aux_length"]
    del form.attributes["_aux_vector"]

    return form

def static_equilibrium(
    topology, kmax=None, tmax=100, eta=1e-6, verbose=False, callback=None
):
    """
    Generate a form diagram in static equilibrium.

    Parameters
    ----------
    topology : :class:`compas_cem.diagrams.TopologyDiagram`
        A topology diagram.
    kmax : ``int``, optional
        The last sequence in the diagram to calculate equilibrium at.
        If ``kmax`` is ``None`` or the number of sequences in the diagram is smaller,
        then ``kmax`` will be ignored and equilibrium will be calculated for all sequences.
        Defaults to ``None``.
    tmax : ``int``, optional
        Maximum number of iterations the algorithm will run for.
        Defaults to ``100``.
    eta : ``float``, optional
        Distance threshold that marks equilibrium convergence.
        This threshold is compared against the sum of distances of the nodes'
        positions from one iteration to the next one.
        If ``eta`` is hit before consuming ``tmax`` iterations, calculations

def __init__(self, drawing, is_thickened=False, thick_sides=8):
    document = Rhino.RhinoDoc.ActiveDoc
    styled_lines = drawing.edges + drawing.loads + drawing.reactions
    self._drawing = drawing
    self._is_thickened = is_thickened
    self._thick_sides = thick_sides

    self._lines = []
    self._points = []
    self._meshes = []
    if is_thickened:
        sides = thick_sides
        node_meshes = [_sphere_mesh(item, sides) for item in drawing.nodes]
        support_meshes = [
            _sphere_mesh(item, sides) for item in drawing.support_nodes
        ]
        edge_meshes = [_pipe_mesh(item, sides) for item in drawing.edges]
        load_meshes = [_arrow_mesh(item, sides) for item in drawing.loads]
        reaction_meshes = [_arrow_mesh(item, sides) for item in drawing.reactions]

        self.node_objects = _model_meshes(document, drawing.nodes, node_meshes)
        self.support_objects = _model_meshes(
            document, drawing.support_nodes, support_meshes
        )
        self.edge_objects = _model_meshes(document, drawing.edges, edge_meshes)
        self.load_objects = _model_meshes(document, drawing.loads, load_meshes)
        self.reaction_objects = _model_meshes(
            document, drawing.reactions, reaction_meshes
        )

        styled_items = drawing.nodes + styled_lines
        meshes = node_meshes + edge_meshes + load_meshes + reaction_meshes
        self._meshes = _preview_meshes(styled_items, meshes)
    else:
        self.node_objects = [_model_point(document, item) for item in drawing.nodes]
        self.support_objects = [
            _model_point(document, item) for item in drawing.support_nodes
        ]
        self.edge_objects = [_model_line(document, item) for item in drawing.edges]
        self.load_objects = [_model_line(document, item) for item in drawing.loads]
        self.reaction_objects = [
            _model_line(document, item) for item in drawing.reactions
        ]

        self._lines = [_preview_line(item) for item in styled_lines]
        self._points = [_preview_point(item) for item in drawing.nodes]

    self._labels = [_preview_label(item) for item in drawing.labels]

    self.clipping_box = _bounding_box(
        self._lines, self._meshes, self._points, self._labels
    )

def bake(self, document):
    """
    Add what the preview draws to a Rhino document, one sublayer per
    category under `COMPAS CEM::Form`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    document :
        The Rhino document to bake into.

    Returns
    -------
    ids :
        The ids of the baked objects.

    Notes
    -----
    Lines bake with their colors and plot weights, and force lines with an
    arrowhead; thickened meshes bake with their colors. The support nodes,
    which repeat nodes, and the labels are not baked.
    """
    drawing = self._drawing
    groups = [
        ("Nodes", drawing.nodes),
        ("Edges", drawing.edges),
        ("Loads", drawing.loads),
        ("Reactions", drawing.reactions),
    ]
    if self._is_thickened:
        records = _mesh_records(groups, self._thick_sides)
    else:
        records = _line_records(groups)
    ids = _bake_records(document, "COMPAS CEM::Form", records)

    return ids

def cross_lines(diagram, nodes):
    """
    The two lines of the cross that marks every given node.

    Parameters
    ----------
    diagram :
        The diagram the nodes belong to, whose extent sizes the crosses.
    nodes :
        The nodes to mark.

    Returns
    -------
    lines :
        Two start and end point pairs per node, at right angles in the XY
        plane, each reaching `LOAD_CROSS_SIZE` of the diagram's bounding-box
        diagonal from the node.

    Notes
    -----
    Every engine that crosses the loaded nodes of a topology draws these lines,
    so the crosses match across them.
    """
    diagonal = _diagram_diagonal(diagram)
    reach = LOAD_CROSS_SIZE * diagonal / sqrt(2.0)

    lines = []
    for node in nodes:
        x, y, z = diagram.node_coordinates(node)
        for sign in (1.0, -1.0):
            start = [x - reach, y - sign * reach, z]
            end = [x + reach, y + sign * reach, z]
            lines.append((start, end))

    return lines

def form_drawing(form, node_keys, edge_keys, settings):
    """
    Style a selection of a form diagram for drawing.

    Parameters
    ----------
    form :
        The form diagram to draw.
    node_keys :
        The nodes to draw, with their loads and reaction forces. If `None`,
        every node is drawn.
    edge_keys :
        The edges to draw. If `None`, every edge is drawn.
    settings :
        The display settings.

    Returns
    -------
    drawing :
        The styled nodes, support nodes, edges, loads, reaction forces, and the
        labels. A category the settings hide is empty.

    Notes
    -----
    Every node is colored by whether it is a support, so the support nodes are
    drawn twice, once among the nodes and once on their own. A load arrow
    always ends at its node, so its head touches the node it loads; a reaction
    ends at its support only when it pushes into it. An edge shown with both
    its key and its force gets one label, `u-v: force`, so the two never
    overlap.
    """
    nodes = list(form.nodes()) if node_keys is None else list(node_keys)
    edges = list(form.edges()) if edge_keys is None else list(edge_keys)
    supports = [node for node in nodes if form.is_node_support(node)]

    sphere_radius = settings.radius_max
    node_points = [_styled_node(form, node, sphere_radius) for node in nodes]
    support_points = [_styled_node(form, node, sphere_radius) for node in supports]

    ratios = _force_ratios(form)
    widths = _spread_ratios(ratios, settings.width_min, settings.width_max)
    radii = _spread_ratios(ratios, settings.radius_min, settings.radius_max)
    edge_lines = []
    for edge in edges:
        key = tuple(edge)
        line = _styled_edge(form, edge, widths[key], radii[key], sphere_radius)
        edge_lines.append(line)

    loads = []
    if settings.show_loads:
        load_shifts = {node: True for node in nodes}
        loads = _force_lines(form, nodes, "load", load_shifts, settings)

    reactions = []
    if settings.show_reactions:
        shifts = reaction_shifts(form, nodes)
        reactions = _force_lines(form, nodes, "support_force", shifts, settings)

    labels = _form_labels(form, nodes, edges, settings)

    drawing = FormDrawing(
        nodes=node_points,
        support_nodes=support_points,
        edges=edge_lines,
        loads=loads,
        reactions=reactions,
        labels=labels,
    )

    return drawing

def reaction_shifts(form, nodes):
    """
    Whether the reaction force at every node points back into its trail.

    Parameters
    ----------
    form :
        The form diagram.
    nodes :
        The nodes to decide the shift of.

    Returns
    -------
    shifts :
        A mapping of nodes to whether the reaction force is shifted.

    Notes
    -----
    A reaction is shifted when the strongest edge meeting the node is in
    compression, so the force reads as pushing against the support rather
    than pulling away from it. A node with no connected edge is never
    shifted, which also keeps the strongest-edge search off an empty set.

    TODO: needs a more robust check for orientation. What is wanted is to
    know whether the force needs a full shift.
    """
    shifts = {}
    for node in nodes:
        forces = [form.edge_force(edge) for edge in form.node_connected_edges(node)]
        if not forces:
            shifts[node] = False
            continue
        shifts[node] = max(forces, key=fabs) < 0.0

    return shifts

def topology_drawing(topology, node_keys, edge_keys, show_keys):
    """
    Style a selection of a topology diagram for drawing.

    Parameters
    ----------
    topology :
        The topology diagram to draw.
    node_keys :
        The nodes to draw, with the crosses of the loaded ones. If `None`,
        every node is drawn.
    edge_keys :
        The edges to draw. If `None`, every edge is drawn.
    show_keys :
        Whether to label the drawn nodes and edges with their keys.

    Returns
    -------
    drawing :
        The styled nodes, origin nodes, support nodes, edges, trail edges,
        deviation edges, trails, load crosses, and the key labels when shown.

    Notes
    -----
    The colors follow the topology plotter's defaults: nodes by type, and
    edges by the state their length or force sets, with auxiliary trails
    apart. Deviation edges are always dashed. A loaded node is marked with a
    cross of two lines at right angles in the XY plane, each reaching
    `LOAD_CROSS_SIZE` of the diagram's bounding-box diagonal from the node.
    Every trail is drawn whole, whatever the edge selection.
    """
    nodes = list(topology.nodes()) if node_keys is None else list(node_keys)
    edges = list(topology.edges()) if edge_keys is None else list(edge_keys)

    node_points = [_topology_node(topology, node) for node in nodes]
    node_styles = list(zip(nodes, node_points))
    origin_points = [
        point for node, point in node_styles if topology.is_node_origin(node)
    ]
    support_points = [
        point for node, point in node_styles if topology.is_node_support(node)
    ]

    auxiliary_trails = {tuple(trail) for trail in topology.auxiliary_trails()}
    edge_lines = [_topology_edge(topology, edge, auxiliary_trails) for edge in edges]
    edge_styles = list(zip(edges, edge_lines))
    trail_lines = [line for edge, line in edge_styles if topology.is_trail_edge(edge)]
    deviation_lines = [
        line for edge, line in edge_styles if topology.is_deviation_edge(edge)
    ]
    trails = _topology_trails(topology, auxiliary_trails)

    loaded_nodes = set(topology.loaded_nodes())
    crossed_nodes = [node for node in nodes if node in loaded_nodes]
    crosses = _load_crosses(topology, crossed_nodes)

    labels = []
    if show_keys:
        labels = _key_labels(topology, nodes, edges)

    drawing = TopologyDrawing(
        nodes=node_points,
        origin_nodes=origin_points,
        support_nodes=support_points,
        edges=edge_lines,
        trail_edges=trail_lines,
        deviation_edges=deviation_lines,
        trails=trails,
        loads=crosses,
        labels=labels,
    )

    return drawing

def check_start_bounds(self, topology):
    """
    Verify that every parameter starts within its bounds.

    Notes
    -----
    NLopt rejects a start value outside the bounds with a bare error. Absolute
    bounds can exclude the start value; relative bounds always contain it.
    """
    for parameter in self.parameters.values():
        start = parameter.start_value(topology)
        bound_low = parameter.bound_low(topology)
        bound_up = parameter.bound_up(topology)
        if bound_low <= start <= bound_up:
            continue
        msg = f"{parameter!r} starts at {start}, outside its bounds [{bound_low}, {bound_up}]."
        raise ValueError(msg)

def solve(
    self,
    topology,
    algorithm="SLSQP",
    grad="AD",
    step_size=1e-6,
    iters=100,
    eps=1e-6,
    kappa=1e-8,
    tmax=100,
    eta=1e-6,
    verbose=False,
):
    """
    Solve a constrained form-finding problem using gradient-based optimization.

    Parameters
    ----------
    topology : :class:`compas_cem.diagrams.TopologyDiagram`
        A topology diagram.
    algorithm : ``str``, optional
        The name of the gradient-based local optimization algorithm to use.
        Only the following local gradient-based optimization algorithms are supported:

        - SLSQP: Sequential Least Squares Programming
        - LBFGS: Low-Storage Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno
        - MMA: Method of Moving Asymptotes
        - TNEWTON: Preconditioned Truncated Newton
        - AUGLAG: Augmented Lagrangian
        - VAR: Limited-Memory Variable-Metric Algorithm

        Defaults to "SLSQP".
        Refer to the NLopt `documentation <https://nlopt.readthedocs.io/en/latest/>`_ for more details on their theoretical underpinnings.
    grad : ``str``, optional
        The method to compute the gradient of the objective function.
        The currently available methods are:

        - AD: Automatic differentiation
        - FD: Finite differences

        Defaults to "AD".
    iters : ``int``, optional
        The maximum number of iterations to run the optimization algorithm for.
        Defaults to ``100``.
    eps : ``float``, optional
        The convergence threshold for the output value of the objective function.
        Defaults to ``1e-6``.
    kappa : ``float``, optional
        The convergence threshold for the norm of the gradient of the objective function.
        Defaults to ``1e-8``.
    step_size : ``float``, optional
        The step size to calculate the gradient of the objective function via finite differences.
        It becomes active only if ``grad="FD"``. It is otherwise ignored by this function.
        Defaults to ``1e-3``.
    tmax : ``int``, optional
        The maximum number of iterations the CEM form-finding algorithm will run for.
        If ``eta`` is hit first, the form-finding algorithm will stop early.
        Defaults to ``100``.
    eta : ``float``, optional
        The numerical converge threshold of the CEM form-finding algorithm.
        If ``tmax`` is hit first, the form-finding algorithm will stop early.
        Defaults to ``1e-6``.
    verbose : ``bool``, optional
        A flag to prints statistics of the optimization process.
        Defaults to ``True``.

    Returns
    -------
    form : :class:`compas_cem.diagrams.FormDiagram`
        A form diagram.
    """
    if verbose:
        print("----------")
        print("Optimization with {} started!".format(algorithm))
        print(
            f"# Parameters: {self.number_of_parameters()}, # Goals {self.number_of_goals()}"
        )

    # test for bad stuff before going any further
    self.check_optimization_sanity()
    self.check_start_bounds(topology)

    # compose gradient and objective functions
    if grad not in ("AD", "FD"):
        raise ValueError(f"Gradient method {grad} is not supported!")
    if grad == "AD":
        if verbose:
            print("Computing gradients using automatic differentiation!")
        x_func = partial(
            self._optimize_form, topology=topology.copy(), tmax=tmax, eta=eta
        )
        grad_func = partial(
            grad_autograd, grad_func=agrad(x_func)
        )  # x, grad, x_func

    elif grad == "FD":
        if verbose:
            print(
                f"Warning: Calculating gradients using finite differences with step size {step_size}. This may take a while..."
            )
        grad_func = self.gradient_func(
            grad_finite_differences, topology.copy(), tmax, eta, step_size
        )

    # grad_func = self.gradient_func(grad_func, topology.copy(), tmax, eta, step_size)
    obj_func = self.objective_func(topology, grad_func, tmax, eta)

    # generate optimization variables
    x = self.optimization_parameters(topology)

    # extract the lower and upper bounds to optimization variables
    bounds_low, bounds_up = self.optimization_bounds(topology)

    # stack keyword arguments
    hyper_parameters = {
        "f": obj_func,
        "algorithm": algorithm,
        "dims": self.number_of_parameters(),
        "bounds_low": bounds_low,
        "bounds_up": bounds_up,
        "iters": iters,
        "eps": eps,
        "ftol": kappa,
    }

    # assemble optimization solver
    solver = nlopt_solver(**hyper_parameters)

    # solve optimization problem
    x_opt = None
    start = time()
    try:
        x_opt = solver.optimize(x)
        if verbose:
            print("Optimization ended correctly!")
    except RoundoffLimited:
        print("Optimization was halted because roundoff errors limited progress")
        print("Results may still be useful though!")
        x_opt = self.optimization_parameters(topology)
    except RuntimeError:
        print("Optimization failed due to a runtime error!")
        print(f"Optimization total runtime: {round(time() - start, 4)} seconds")
        return static_equilibrium(topology)

    # fetch last optimum value of loss function
    time_opt = time() - start
    loss_opt = solver.last_optimum_value()
    evals = solver.get_numevals()
    status = nlopt_status(solver.last_optimize_result())

    # set optimizer attributes
    self.time_opt = time_opt
    self.x_opt = x_opt
    self.penalty = loss_opt
    self.evals = evals
    self.status = status

    # set norm of the gradient
    # NOTE: np.zeros is a dummy array (signature requirement set by nlopt)
    self.gradient = grad_func(x_opt, np.zeros(x_opt.size))
    self.gradient_norm = np.linalg.norm(self.gradient)

    if verbose:
        print(f"Optimization total runtime: {round(time_opt, 6)} seconds")
        print("Number of evaluations incurred: {}".format(evals))
        print(f"Final value of the objective function: {round(loss_opt, 6)}")
        print(
            f"Norm of the gradient of the objective function: {round(self.gradient_norm, 6)}"
        )
        print(f"Optimization status: {status}".format(status))
        print("----------")

    # exit like a champion
    return static_equilibrium(topology)

def grad_finite_differences(x, grad, x_func, step_size, **kwargs):
    """
    Approximate the gradient of a blackbox function using forward finite differences.
    This function updates grad in place.
    """
    fx0 = x_func(x)
    # NOTE: We make an editable copy of x because NLOpt makes x a read-only vector
    _x = np.copy(x)

    for i in range(len(x)):
        _xi = _x[i]
        _x[i] += step_size

        fx1 = x_func(_x)

        delta_fx = (fx1 - fx0) / step_size
        grad[i] = delta_fx
        _x[i] = _xi

    return grad

def nlopt_solver(f, algorithm, dims, bounds_up, bounds_low, iters, eps, ftol):
    """
    Wrapper around a typical nlopt solver routine.
    """
    solver = opt(nlopt_algorithm(algorithm), dims)

    if algorithm == "AUGLAG":
        solver.set_local_optimizer(opt(nlopt_algorithm("VAR"), dims))

    if algorithm in ("VAR", "TNEWTON"):
        solver.set_vector_storage(100)  # Defaults to 10 or to 10 MiB of data

    if algorithm == "MMA":
        solver.set_param("inner_maxeval", 5)

    solver.set_lower_bounds(bounds_low)
    solver.set_upper_bounds(bounds_up)

    solver.set_maxeval(iters)

    if ftol is not None:
        # relative difference between two consecutive iterations
        # ftol_abs as per recommendation in the NLOpt docs
        solver.set_ftol_abs(ftol)

    if eps is not None:
        solver.set_stopval(eps)

    solver.set_min_objective(f)

    return solver

    results = {}

        3: "NLOPT_FTOL_REACHED",
        4: "NLOPT_XTOL_REACHED",

        -4: "NLOPT_ROUNDOFF_LIMITED",
        -5: "NLOPT_FORCED_STOP",
    }

    results.update(success)
    results.update(failure)

    return results[constant]

def edge_widths(self):
    """
    The width to draw every edge with.

    Returns
    -------
    widths :
        A mapping of edges to widths.

    Notes
    -----
    A single width is used for every edge unless a pair of bounds is given,
    in which case the absolute edge forces are spread linearly over them.
    """
    edgewidth = self.edgewidth

    if not isinstance(edgewidth, (tuple, list)):
        return {edge: edgewidth for edge in self.diagram.edges()}

    low, high = edgewidth
    forces = [fabs(self.diagram.edge_force(edge)) for edge in self.diagram.edges()]
    forcemin = min(forces)
    forcemax = max(forces)

    widths = {}
    for edge in self.diagram.edges():
        force = fabs(self.diagram.edge_force(edge))
        try:
            ratio = (force - forcemin) / (forcemax - forcemin)
        except ZeroDivisionError:
            ratio = 1.0
        widths[edge] = (1.0 - ratio) * low + ratio * high

    return widths

def draw_forces(self):
    """
    Draw the loaded nodes as crosses inscribed in a circle.

    Notes
    -----
    The crosses are drawn straight onto the canvas rather than added to the
    scene, because a line scene object fixes its own stacking order and
    would end up underneath the opaque node markers.
    """
    if not self.show_loads:
        return

    topology = self.topology
    radius = self._node_radius()

    flips = (-1, 1)
    angle = pi / 4.0
    axis = [0.0, 0.0, 1.0]

    segments = []
    for node in topology.loaded_nodes():
        xyz = topology.node_coordinates(node)

        for flip in flips:
            line = Line(*[add_vectors(xyz, [radius * f, 0.0, 0.0]) for f in flips])
            rotation = Rotation.from_axis_and_angle(
                axis=axis, angle=flip * angle, point=xyz
            )
            line.transform(rotation)

            segments.append([line.start[:2], line.end[:2]])

    if not segments:
        return

    collection = LineCollection(
        segments,
        linewidths=0.3,
        colors=[to_rgb(Color.black())] * len(segments),
        zorder=4000,
    )
    self.axes.add_collection(collection)
    self._mpl_objects.append(collection)

def edge_colors(self):
    """
    Color the edges by their type.

    Notes
    -----
    Direct and indirect deviation edges are told apart only once the trails
    have been built, because the distinction is drawn from the sequence the
    two end nodes belong to.
    """
    topology = self.topology
    colors = {}

    for edge in topology.edges():
        if topology.is_auxiliary_trail_edge(edge):
            colors[edge] = self.edgecolor_auxiliary
        elif topology.is_trail_edge(edge):
            colors[edge] = self.edgecolor_trail
        elif topology.has_trails() and topology.is_indirect_deviation_edge(edge):
            colors[edge] = self.edgecolor_deviation_indirect
        else:
            colors[edge] = self.edgecolor_deviation

    return colors

def edge_textlabel_formatters(self):
    """
    The supported edge label tags and the formatter of each.
    """
    formatters = super(TopologyDiagramObject, self).edge_textlabel_formatters()
    precision = self.float_precision
    topology = self.topology

    def state_format(edge):
        if topology.is_trail_edge(edge):
            parameter = topology.edge_length_2(edge)
        else:
            parameter = topology.edge_force(edge)
        return "{0:.{1}}".format(copysign(1.00, parameter), precision)

    def type_format(edge):
        return "{}".format(topology.edge_attribute(edge, "type"))

    formatters.update({"state": state_format, "type": type_format})

    return formatters

from compas_cem.optimization import TrailEdgeForceGoal

# Instantiate a topology diagram

topology = TopologyDiagram()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Add nodes
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

width = 4.0
height = width / 2

topology.add_node(Node(1, [-width / 2.0, height, 0.0]))
topology.add_node(Node(2, [width / 2.0, height, 0.0]))
topology.add_node(Node(3, [0.0, height / 2.5, 0.0]))
topology.add_node(Node(4, [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Add edges
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

topology.add_edge(TrailEdge(3, 4, length=-height / 2))
topology.add_edge(DeviationEdge(1, 3, force=-sqrt(4.0)))
topology.add_edge(DeviationEdge(2, 3, force=-sqrt(2.0)))
topology.add_edge(DeviationEdge(1, 2, force=2.0))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Add supports
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

topology.add_support(NodeSupport(4))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Add loads
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

topology.add_load(NodeLoad(1, [0.0, -1.0, 0.0]))
topology.add_load(NodeLoad(2, [0.0, -1.0, 0.0]))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Build trails and auto generate auxiliary trails
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

topology.build_trails(auxiliary_trails=True)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compute a state of static equilibrium
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

form = static_equilibrium(topology, eta=1e-5, tmax=100)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Minimize the forces in the axiliary trails
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

optimizer = Optimizer()

# add goal goals
for edge in topology.auxiliary_trail_edges():
    optimizer.add_goal(TrailEdgeForceGoal(edge, force=0.0))
    optimizer.add_goal(TrailEdgeForceGoal(edge, force=0.0))

# add parameters
optimizer.add_parameter(DeviationEdgeParameter((1, 2), 1.0, 10.0))
optimizer.add_parameter(DeviationEdgeParameter((1, 3), 1.0, 10.0))
optimizer.add_parameter(DeviationEdgeParameter((2, 3), 10.0, 1.0))

# optimize
form_opt = optimizer.solve(topology, "SLSQP", iters=100, eps=1e-6, verbose=True)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot results
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ns = 0.3
shift = width * 1.2
plotter = Plotter(figsize=(16.0, 9.0))

# plot topology diagram
plotter.add(topology, nodesize=ns, show_nodetext=True, nodetext="key")

# plot translated form diagram

plotter.add(
    form.transformed(T),
    nodesize=ns,
    show_nodetext=True,
    nodetext="key",
    show_edgetext=True,
    edgetext="force",
)

# plot translated optimized form diagram
T = Translation.from_vector([shift * 2.0, 0.0, 0.0])
plotter.add(
    form_opt.transformed(T),
    nodesize=ns,
    show_nodetext=True,
    nodetext="key",
    show_edgetext=True,
    edgetext="force",
)

# show scene
plotter.zoom_extents(padding=-1.2)
plotter.show()

from math import cos
from math import pi
from math import sin

import numpy as np
from compas.geometry import Translation
from compas.itertools import pairwise

from compas_cem.diagrams import TopologyDiagram
from compas_cem.elements import DeviationEdge
from compas_cem.elements import Node
from compas_cem.equilibrium import static_equilibrium
from compas_cem.optimization import DeviationEdgeParameter
from compas_cem.optimization import Optimizer
from compas_cem.optimization import TrailEdgeForceGoal
from compas_cem.plotters import Plotter

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create a topology diagram
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# geometry parameters
diameter = 1.0
num_sides = 16  # only even numbers
appendix_length = 0.10
tension_force = 1.0
compression_force = -0.5
bound = 2.0
grad_method = "AD"

# test number of subdivisions is even
assert num_sides % 2 == 0

# create a topology diagram
topology = TopologyDiagram()

# create nodes, removing last
thetas = np.linspace(0.0, 2 * pi, num_sides + 1)[:-1]
radius = diameter / 2.0

for i, theta in enumerate(thetas):
    x = radius * cos(theta)
    y = radius * sin(theta)

    # nodes in the wheel
    topology.add_node(Node(i, [x, y, 0.0]))

# deviation edges in the perimeter of the wheel tension
for u, v in pairwise(list(range(num_sides)) + [0]):
    topology.add_edge(DeviationEdge(u, v, force=tension_force))

# internal deviation edges are in compression
half_num_sides = num_sides / 2.0

for u in range(int(half_num_sides)):
    v = int(u + half_num_sides)
    topology.add_edge(DeviationEdge(u, v, force=compression_force))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate trails and auto generate auxiliary trails
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

topology.auxiliary_trail_length = appendix_length * -1.0
topology.build_trails(auxiliary_trails=True)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compute a state of static equilibrium
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

form = static_equilibrium(topology, eta=1e-6, tmax=100)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Optimization
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# create optimizer
opt = Optimizer()

# add goal: force in axiliary trail edges should be zero
for edge in topology.auxiliary_trail_edges():
    opt.add_goal(TrailEdgeForceGoal(edge, force=0.0))

# add optimization parameters
# the forces in all the deviation edges are allowed to change
for edge in topology.deviation_edges():
    opt.add_parameter(DeviationEdgeParameter(edge, bound, bound))

# optimize
form_opt = opt.solve(topology, algorithm="LBFGS", grad=grad_method, verbose=True)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot results
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ns = 0.45
shift = diameter * 1.4
plotter = Plotter(figsize=(16.0, 9.0))

# plot topology diagram
plotter.add(topology, nodesize=ns)

# plot translated form diagram
T = Translation.from_vector([shift, 0.0, 0.0])
plotter.add(form.transformed(T), nodesize=ns)

# plot translated optimized form diagram
T = Translation.from_vector([shift * 2.0, 0.0, 0.0])
plotter.add(form_opt.transformed(T), nodesize=ns)

# show scene
plotter.zoom_extents(padding=-0.3)
plotter.show()
